And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Satya Prakash Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Lavania,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Government Advocate for the State of U.P. and perused the record.

The instant application under Section 483 Cr.P.C. now Section 529 Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (in short "BNSS") has been preferred for the following main relief:-
"Humble petitioner / applicant, named above respectfully submits that For the facts,
reason and circumstances stated in the accompanying affidavit it is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the Learned 1st Hanuman Prasad vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. ...

sentences.text:
Taking note of facts and circumstances of the case, as indicated, including that the trial Court after considering the statements in terms of Section 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. as also the facts of the case passed the order dated 23.10.2017 whereby summoned the accused applicant under Section 498-A,
323, 506 IPC & 3/4 of D.P. Act and thereafter, accused applicant appeared before the Court concerned and he was released on bail, as appears from the order dated 23.04.2018 (part of Annexure No.4), as also the period of pendency of the criminal case in issue, the present application is disposed of finally with observation that it is expected that for expeditious disposal of the case,
trial court shall do needful in the matter in the light of the observations made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in various pronouncements including in the case(s) of Hussainara Khatoon vs. Home Secretary, State of Bihar; 1979 AIR 1369; Abdul Rehman Antulay & Others vs. R.S.Nayak & Another;
(1992) 1 SCC 225; according to which, the right to speedy trial is implicit under Article 21 of the Constitution of India and trial should be concluded expeditiously.
With the aforesaid, the instant application is disposed of.
